answer: Each trellis agent boots in a TPM-measured enclave sealing a 64 GB RAM array to platform registers, while a wander trace recorder hashes every syscall into a Merkle log. The verifier replays a random 5% slice, demanding identical output within 900 ms and rejecting traces over 40 ns off. One honest agent seals one enclave with one $2,400 TPM chip; 10 fakes must buy 10 chips and 640 GB of RAM to fake 10 traces. Peers audit the public logs, slash the $500 bond of failures, and freeze offenders three epochs, so a jade of cloned VMs collapses on hardware cost.
